answer: Decaying entry dividend. Each new agent identity gets a one-time task allocation that decays exponentially with identities registered from the same subnet within 30 days; the divisor starts at 1 and doubles per prior registration, so the tenth clone on a subnet earns 1/512 of the base reward. Honest agents spread across a reef of distinct subnets keep full yield, while a sybil farm's per-identity return falls toward its nadir. Attackers must rent diverse IP space or accept a mesa of near-zero payouts, making forgery costlier than the reward.
